jobs.occupation: Senior Product Specialist, Fermented High Protein - Aarhus
jobs.description:
Is your mind set on innovation and developing the next generation of high-protein dairy products?

Are you looking for a role where you can combine deep process expertise, product development excellence and capability building to shape the future of Fermented High Protein products?

This could be your chance to join a leading global dairy company that takes innovation, product superiority and process excellence seriously. The job location is based in our Arla Innovation Centre in Aarhus.

“You will be part of our Fermented High Protein Innovation team, helping to create superior products, strengthen our process capabilities and build the knowledge foundations needed for future growth. So, if you are passionate about working in a fast-paced international environment and want to make a significant impact on the future of Skyr, Quark, Greek yoghurt and other high-protein dairy platforms, this could be your next career move_,” says Associate Director – High Protein Fermented Innovation, Jorden Naseby

Create Product & Process Excellence for Fermented High Protein Innovation

We are looking to strengthen process capability across our Fermented High Protein organisation.

Your main goal is to combine hands-on product development with process leadership, helping the team make robust, data-driven decisions and creating the tools, knowledge and best practices needed to accelerate innovation. You will work closely with Innovation, Science, Operations, Quality, Packaging, Marketing and Supply Chain teams across Europe.

This position places you in a unique role where you will influence both today's products and the future capability of the organisation. You will drive deep process development expertise to support capex investment projects across our network of production sites.

Key responsibilities include:

• Leading complex product and process development projects from concept to launch.

• Acting as a product and process expert across fermented high-protein product platforms including Skyr, Quark, yoghurt and emerging technologies.

• Driving laboratory, pilot and industrial trials and translating technical findings into clear business recommendations.

• Identifying and solving complex product quality, stability and process challenges.

• Leading knowledge in process and product interactions within the team.

• Developing technical playbooks, guidelines, troubleshooting tools and best-practice ways of working.

• Establishing structured approaches for experimentation, data interpretation and root-cause analysis.

• Contributing to future product and technology roadmaps within Fermented High Protein.

• Supporting external manufacturing, supplier collaborations and Contract Manufacturing activities where specialist technical expertise is required.

Inventive, product and processing expert, strong and able to challenge the status quo.

If you hold a degree in Food Science, Dairy Technology, Food Engineering or a related discipline, and have significant experience in product & process development within dairy or food manufacturing, you may have the credentials we are looking for.

You are passionate about applying science to solve real business challenges and have a proven ability to translate technical complexity into practical solutions.

Experience within fermented dairy products, high-protein products, fermentation, process development & large-scale manufacturing is a necessity.

You are comfortable influencing without authority and can work effectively across multiple functions, sites and cultures. You enjoy sharing knowledge and helping others develop technical confidence and capability.

This role requires:

• Technical leadership in process and site capabilities across the network.

• Strong product and process development expertise.

• Analytical and data-driven decision making.

• Curiosity and a continuous improvement mindset.

• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.

• The ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

• Fluency in English, written and spoken.

Finally, you build strong relationships, challenge constructively and thrive in an environment where innovation, learning and collaboration are valued.

Application & Contact

If you want to seize this opportunity to help shape the future of Fermented High Protein Innovation and accelerate your career, then please apply as soon as possible.

We process applications on a continuous basis and close the posting once the right candidate has been found.

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

Retire the ERP.

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers—automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Keyshot. People don't just use Light—they enjoy it.

We're an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you're excited to modernize how the world runs money—one workflow at a time—you're in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors and advised by industry titans, we're building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

This Integrations Engineer role

Light is only as powerful as the systems it connects to. Money doesn't move because we say so—it moves because we speak the language of the bank, the e-invoicing network, and the planning tool on the other side, correctly, every time, for every customer entity. This role owns that layer: the interaction surface between Light and the rest of the financial world.

You'll build and operate the integrations that let Light plug into multi-tenant banking APIs (J.P. Morgan, HSBC, and peers), global e-invoicing networks, and tax platforms and more. This is backend-heavy, data-integrity-critical work where a dropped message or a silent reconciliation mismatch is not an acceptable outcome. You'll design the abstractions that turn a dozen incompatible partner APIs into one coherent internal model, and you'll keep those abstractions honest as partners change their specs underneath you.

What you'll work on:

• 
Bank connectivity. Build against corporate banking and payments APIs—account information, payment initiation, status reporting, FX—across providers like J.P. Morgan Payments and HSBC. Handle the realities of bank integrations: certificate-based and mTLS auth, OAuth flows, ISO 20022 (pain/pacs/camt) and legacy MT formats, sandbox-to-production parity, and rate limits that assume you're a bank, not a startup.

• 
Multi-tenancy done right. Our customers are many legal entities operating in many countries. You'll design integrations where credentials, configuration, and data are isolated per tenant, where onboarding a new entity is a workflow rather than a code change, and where one customer's failure never leaks into another's.

• 
Global e-invoicing. Connect Light to e-invoicing networks and country-specific mandates (Peppol and the growing set of national clearance and reporting regimes). Map between formats, manage compliance-driven edge cases, and keep delivery auditable.

• 
Tax platforms for statutory filing, US sales tax and much more.

• 
Reliability and reconciliation. Idempotency, retries, webhook and polling strategies, dead-letter handling, and end-to-end reconciliation so that what we think happened and what actually happened always agree.

Your qualifications

4-6 years of experience ideally, plus…

You build things. Not prototypes, not demos. Working software in production, doing something real for real users. This is the non-negotiable.

You've built integrations against unforgiving external systems. APIs you don't control, that fail in ways the docs don't mention, where correctness is contractual. You know how to defend a system against a partner that returns a 200 with an error in the body.

You know banking and payments APIs. Direct, hands-on experience with corporate banking, treasury, or payments APIs is what sets the strongest candidates apart. Experience integrating J.P. Morgan or HSBC specifically—their developer platforms, auth models, and payment and reporting APIs—is highly valuable and a genuine differentiator for this role. Familiarity with ISO 20022, SWIFT, virtual accounts, or open banking is a strong signal.

You are excited about AI. You use AI tooling efficiently to improve your work. At Light, a lot of code is written with AI, which means the hard part is increasingly the thinking: deciding what to build, reviewing what comes back, and catching where the model is confidently wrong. You know when AI speeds you up, when it's likely to mislead you, and how to lean on it while staying fully responsible for what ships.

You're comfortable across the stack. You don't need to be a specialist in everything, but you can't have a lane you refuse to leave. Our stack is Kotlin and React, and this role leans backend. If you're strong on the backend and curious about the rest, that works.

You care about data integrity. You think about the person on the other end and the money moving between them. You notice when a flow is correct but fragile, and you act on it.

You ship early and often. Small batches. Learn. Go again. You'd rather put something real in front of a customer than spend another week perfecting it in isolation.

Bonus points

• 
Experience in fintech or systems where data integrity is non-negotiable

• 
Familiarity with accounting concepts: debits, credits, reconciliation

• 
Experience with e-invoicing standards or country-specific compliance regimes

• 
Background in high-growth startups where everything was still being figured out

Our Tech Stack

We build on AWS, with a Kotlin backend, a React frontend, and infrastructure managed in Terraform. It's a real production system that global finance teams depend on every day. The integration layer you'll own sits squarely in the Kotlin backend, talking to a long list of external partners. You don't need to have used every piece of it. You do need to be comfortable in this kind of environment: real scale, real customers, real stakes.

The good stuff

In addition to being part of a great team and working in a really fun and innovative environment, we offer:

• 
A competitive salary + potential stock options

• 
25 days of annual leave + public holidays in the country where you are based

• 
Regular socials and company off-sites

• 
A huge opportunity for career growth as you'll help shape a market-defining product

The famous last words

Working at Light means you're embarking on an exciting journey to reshape the future of multinational financial operations. Our cheat-code is that we've built something like this before—and are now doing it again, only better. Our goal is to make global finance effortless and empower companies to make informed decisions.

Join the rocket ship while it's taking off.

Working at

Light

Light is the new way to run multinational finances for modern technology companies. Run AR, AP, expenses, bookkeeping, and financial reporting automatically across all your entities — without the chaos of multiple systems. Crafted and built by the designers and engineers behind world-class companies like Spotify, X, AWS, Klarna, Google and Shopify, we empower multinational finances with a joyful user experience like no other.

JOIN Terotech

Ready for a career that's challenging, fun, and ever changing?

Terotech has your back on maintaining your equipment.

Working at Terotech

At Terotech, you do more than maintain equipment - you keep large assets running that support critical infrastructure.

We're 50+ people based in Esbjerg, working in Denmark and internationally. Oil & gas, energy, manufacturing - all industries where downtime isn't an option. You learn fast, solve real problems, and see results immediately.

A Place You'll Want to Stay

We work hard - but the industries we serve demand it. That said, we believe work should be somewhere you want to show up. Where colleagues become friends, and people actually care about how your week went.

We meet by the coffee machine. We solve problems as a team. We celebrate wins and support each other continually. The social side isn't extra, but part of our DNA.

Here's something we're proud of: People who've left for other opportunities often stay in touch. Some come back. A few have said they missed the people and culture as much as the work itself. That's the kind of workplace we want to keep building.

Considering a career in Terotech?

We hire for technical skill and personal fit. You need to be a team player who takes initiative, follows through, and speaks up when something isn't right. Our culture is built on five core values: curiosity, openness, empathy, trust, and integrity. This is what you can expect from us, and what we expect from you.

Curiosity

means we keep learning - from each other, and from the problems we solve. We don't just execute tasks, we're curious about understanding our client's world.

Openness

shows in how we communicate. We say what we mean, admit when we don't know something, and share knowledge freely. No hidden agendas.

Empathy

means we see the person, not just the role. Good maintenance work starts with understanding what actually matters to the people involved.

Trust

is earned through follow-through. We do what we say we'll do. We honor the trust clients place in us when they hand over responsibility for their operations.

Integrity

means we speak up when something isn't right - whether it's a safety issue, an unsound plan, or a colleague who needs support.

our People

Maintenance engineers

who’ve kept industrial facilities running for year, both offshore and onshore.

Mechanics and technicians

with decades of hands-on experience in high-stakes environments.

Electricians

who can troubleshoot complex systems under pressure.

Asset Management specialists

who turn data into decisions.

Programmers and data analysts

who build systems people want use.

Project managers

who keep everything on track.

Considering a career in Terotech?

Check our open positions

We’re always looking for talented colleagues who share our values and want to do meaningful work. If you think you’d be a good fit, send us an unsolicited application to Jannie Schlosser Lund at jsl@tero.tech and tell us what you’re good at and why you want to be part of our team.

Maintenance Engineer

We are looking for an ambitious new colleague to join our young and dynamic team. You are motivated by making a real difference within maintenance and asset management and are eager to help organizations improve the performance and sustainability of their physical assets. In this role, you will have the opportunity to develop into a leading advisor within the field. You will work hands-on with our solutions, taking them from concept to implementation and seeing the results delivered directly at both existing and future client sites.

Location

Esbjerg, Denmark

Full-time

Institut for Retsmedicin på Aarhus Universitets sundhedsvidenskabelige fakultet søger en klinisk adjunkt i retsmedicin pr. 1. januar 2027 eller snarest muligt derefter. Stillingen er en tidsbegrænset honorarstilling, som udløber når hoveduddannelsesforløbet til speciallæge i retsmedicin afsluttes.

Som klinisk adjunkt ved Institut for Retsmedicin bliver du en del af en arbejdsplads med dedikerede og specialiserede medarbejdere. Alle deler et mål om at forebygge og opklare kriminalitet, ulykker, for tidlig død og selvmord gennem forskning, undervisning og retsmedicinske undersøgelser. Instituttet hører under det sundhedsvidenskabelige fakultet Health på Aarhus Universitet og beskæftiger 70 medarbejdere fordelt på to afdelinger, der leverer uvildig og evidensbaseret myndighedsbetjening for politiet. Afdeling for Retskemi identificerer og bestemmer renheden af euforiserende stoffer og lægemidler i biologisk materiale og i genstande beslaglagt af politiet. Afdeling for Retspatologi foretager retslægelige obduktioner, findestedsundersøgelser og kliniske retsmedicinske undersøgelser. Begge afdelinger er enten akkrediteret efter kvalitetsstandarderne ISO 17025 eller ISO 17020. Derudover har instituttet tre forskningsenheder, der fokuserer på bioanalytisk kemi, retsmedicinsk billeddiagnostik og klinisk retsmedicin. De ansatte bevæger sig i krydsfeltet mellem myndighedsbetjeningen og grund- og anvendt forskning, og instituttet har et skrapt fokus på det gode arbejdsmiljø, som er en forudsætning for høj kvalitet i løsningen af opgaver på alle niveauer. Du kan læse mere om instituttet her og om fakultetet her.

Dine arbejdsopgaver
Som klinisk adjunkt i retsmedicin bidrager du til udvikling af instituttets forsknings- og undervisningsmiljø, hvor du gennemfører undervisning inden for instituttets undervisningsområder. I din undervisning sikrer du en høj faglig og didaktisk standard.

Dine opgaver vil primært bestå af:

• Forskningsopgaver
• Forberedelse af og gennemførelse af undervisning
• Eksamensforpligtigelse, herunder mundtlige eksaminationer
• I begrænset omfang vejledning af bachelor- og kandidatstuderende
• Øvrige opgaver
Du refererer til institutleder Christian Lindholst.

Ansættelse som klinisk adjunkt kræver samtidigt ansættelse i et hoveduddannelsesforløb til speciallæge inden for retsmedicin.

Dine kompetencer
Du har en lægevidenskabelig kandidateksamen og erfaring inden for det retsmedicinske fagområde. Du har videnskabelige kvalifikationer på ph.d.-niveau og erfaring med forskningsvejledning på universitetsniveau. Du vil varetage undervisning af studerende i kliniske fag og evner at opbygge tillidsfulde relationer til både studerende, kolleger og samarbejdspartnere. Som underviser formidler du den nyeste og relevante viden engageret, klart og tydeligt.

Som person har du gode samarbejdsevner, er imødekommende og evner at bidrage til et godt arbejdsmiljø.

Vi forventer du taler og skriver flydende engelsk.

For at kunne blive bedømt kvalificeret som klinisk adjunkt, skal du opfylde disse faglige kriterier.

For at komme i betragtning til stillingen skal ansøger opfylde de formelle krav til videnskabelige ansættelser ved Aarhus Universitet og indsende alt relevant ansøgningsmateriale inden ansøgningsfristen. Ansøgninger, der er væsentligt mangelfulde, vil ikke indgå i den videre vurdering.

Du vil indgå i den retsmedicinske vagtordning.

Indhentelse af en tilfredsstillende straffeattest og børneattest er en forudsætning for ansættelse i stillingen. 

Spørgsmål til stillingen
Har du spørgsmål til stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte institutleder, Christian Lindholst tlf.: +45 8716 7500.

Arbejdsstedet er Institut for Retsmedicin, Palle Juul-Jensens Boulevard 43, 8200 Aarhus N, Danmark.

Vi forventer at afholde samtaler i december 2026. 

Ansættelsesgrundlag
• Kvalifikationskrav og stillingsindhold er yderligere beskrevet i stillingsstrukturen for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter.
• Ansættelse som klinisk adjunkt forudsætter, at vedkommende er erklæret kvalificeret hertil af et bedømmelsesudvalg. 
• Det er en forudsætning, at den pågældende har påbegyndt et hoveduddannelsesforløb til speciallæge.
• Ansættelse og aflønning sker i henhold til Cirkulære om aftale om kliniske adjunkter ved universiteter under Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet.
Ansøgning
Din ansøgning skal indeholde følgende:

• Ansøgning
• Curriculum Vitae
• Eksamensbevis
• Skabelon til ansøger - klinisk adjunkt skal udfyldes og uploades under feltet ’Skabelon til ansøger’ 
• Publikationsliste
• Undervisningsportfolio. Vi henviser til Vejledning til anvendelse af undervisningsportfolio
• 3 af de for stillingen mest relevante publikationer kan medsendes (valgfrit)
• Forskningsplan, som fremgår af 'Skabelon til ansøger – klinisk adjunkt', kan også medsendes separat (valgfrit)
• Medforfattererklæring kan medsendes (valgfrit)
• Referencer/anbefalinger kan uploades særskilt i e-rekrutteringssystemet (valgfrit)
Vi henviser til fakultetets Vejledning for ansøgere.

Aarhus Universitet vil være en attraktiv og inspirerende arbejdsplads for alle og ønsker en kultur, hvor hver enkelt kan udfolde og udvikle sig. Vi ser ligestilling og diversitet som en styrke og opfordrer derfor alle interesserede til at ansøge.

Ansøgning sendes via Aarhus Universitets rekrutteringssystem, som kan tilgås under stillingsopslaget på Aarhus Universitets hjemmeside.

jobs.occupation: 14 postdoctoral fellowships to the BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme
jobs.description:
BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme
 The BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme at the University of Copenhagen is seeking 14 highly motivated and dynamic postdoc fellows to commence the BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme on 1 September 2027.

  The BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation with the ambition to train fellows in translational medicine, mentored by fully committed and top-level professionals in basic biomedical research, a clinical environment and the life science industry. The programme constitutes a clear career path for candidates whose ambition is to bridge the gap between research, patient care and the life science industry and for those wishing to become pioneering leaders in the field of translational medicine.

  The BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme expects to appoint 7 fellows with an MD background and 7 fellows with an MSc background. The fellow will be appointed in the lab of the basic mentor either at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND) or the Faculty of SCIENCE (SCIENCE), UCPH.

  Application deadline is 9 February 2027, at 23:59 CET. Appointed fellows are expected to participate in a two-day Boot Camp on 9-10 September 2027. Mentors are expected to participate on 9 September 2027.

  Translational research project
 Your research project must cover the early translational stages T₀ (Disease modelling, Omics studies, Basic Research) -T₁ (Biomarker discovery, Target development, Preclinical development) and should bridge a basic biomedical research environment and a clinical research environment, making the research project interdisciplinary in its nature. The project may also cover early T₂ (First in human, phase 1 clinical trials, phase 2 clinical trials, phase 2b clinical trials), but this is not a requirement. 

  Your project must be at the postdoctoral level, should address a relevant medical challenge and should be ambitious yet feasible within the timeframe of two years. Your research project must be developed in collaboration with your Mentor Team and is an important part of the recruitment process to become a BRIDGE Fellow.

  Appointed fellows spend 80% of their time on individual translational research projects mentored by a Mentor Team consisting of a basic biomedical scientist from a SUND or SCIENCE Department or Centre, and a clinical scientist from a hospital in the Capital Region of Denmark or Region Zealand and/or from the life science industry. Additional mentors from other departments and universities in Denmark are encouraged if relevant.

  Academic Curriculum
 The BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme provides fellows with the ability to translate insights from basic research into the clinical sciences and/or the life science industry, and vice versa, and the competences to manage essential collaboration between disciplines.

  A uniquely developed 55 days Academic Curriculum has been designed by top-professional experts and figures as a mandatory, integral, and important part of the BRIDGE programme. 

  The Academic Curriculum covers the translational stages T₀ (Population/clinic to lab feedback, disease modelling -omic studies, basic research), T₁ (Biomarker discovery, target development, pre-clinical development) and border to early T₂ (First in human, phase 1 clinical trials, phase 2 clinical trials, phase 2b clinical trials). 

  In addition, courses also include generic skills such as research management, ethics, research communication and successful grant writing. The Academic Curriculum and additional events such as the Boot Camp, Academic Afternoons, Alumni Event comprise 20% of fellows’ time. The fellows should therefore not be imposed teaching obligations during their fellowship.

  Eligibility
 Future BRIDGE Fellows must hold one of the following: 

   	
• An MD and a PhD degree or equivalent (proof of an appointment that requires doctoral equivalency). Specialist training is no hindrance to apply, and medical training is appreciated.    	
• An MSc and a PhD degree or equivalent (BSc integrated PhD) within a relevant discipline such as veterinary science, biology, biochemistry, molecular biology, bioinformatics, pharmacy, dentistry, or medical engineering.   The following requirements must also be met:

  The PhD degree should have been obtained no more than eight years before the application deadline. Any documented periods of leave will be accepted as extensions of this time limit (maternity leave, paternity leave, family care leave, illness, military service, etc.).

  As a current PhD student, you may apply if you and your supervisor expect your thesis to be submitted and defended prior to project commencement on 1 September 2027.  You must attach a declaration from your supervisor stating that your thesis will be submitted and defended prior to project commencement on 1 September 2027.

  In Denmark, you can hold postdoc positions for no more than a total of four years at one university. Accordingly, no more than two years of postdoc experience based at one of the departments at UCPH prior to programme enrolment is allowed. Any documented periods of leave will be accepted as extensions of this time limit (parental leave, family care leave, illness, military service, etc.). Please find more information about the 'four-year rule' for postdocs (Danish legislation) under 'Eligibility and conditions' and about the applicable governmental jurisdiction here.

  Mentor Teams
 The applicant must apply for the programme in cooperation with a Mentor Team consisting of a minimum of two mentors.

  A Mentor Team requires a mentor representing 1) the basic biomedical science from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND) or the Faculty of SCIENCE (SCIENCE), UCPH, and 2) clinical science from the Capital Region of Denmark or Region Zealand and/or 3) the life science industry environment in Denmark. A life science industry mentor is highly encouraged to enter the Mentor Team.

  We also encourage larger mentor teams with additional mentors from Technical University of Denmark (DTU), or other universities or research institutions, if relevant. 

  Incorporating a mentor from SUND or SCIENCE, UCPH, into the Mentor Team is mandatory. If a mentor acts as a third, fourth or fifth mentor – accompanying a basic and clinical mentor – that mentor may reside outside Denmark.

  NOTE: One can only be a mentor for maximum two candidates for each call. 

  Qualifications
 As a BRIDGE fellow, you are highly motivated to participate in the Academic Curriculum, to be mentored by senior researchers, network and cooperate with other BRIDGE Fellows and you see yourself as an ambitious scientist who will work on bridging the gaps between research, medical treatment and/or the life science industry.

  We expect BRIDGE Fellows to be scientifically independent, showing a high degree of academic maturity. This means that they will have:

   	
• An enthusiastic interest in a translational research project co-designed with a Mentor Team and be a good match with a committed Mentor Team 	
• A strong CV, having published peer reviewed original manuscripts in high-quality journals with minimum one first author paper and presented at international conferences 	
• The ability to manage one’s own academic research and associated activities 	
• Experience with project management 	
• Experience with research supervision of more junior researchers (pre-graduate or PhD students) or clinicians  	
• Excellent interpersonal skills and leadership, including the ability to communicate research ideas and results in a clear and logical way and the ability to interact with peers and the broader research community confidently and effectively   How to apply
 As a BRIDGE fellow, you will be working on a translational research project co-designed with a Mentor Team. As such, the first step in the application process is to connect with a Mentor Team.

  If you are not already in contact with an eligible Mentor Team, we recommend that you:

   	
• Contact a (i) basic biomedical researcher from SUND or SCIENCE, UCPH, a (ii) clinical scientist from a hospital in the Capital Region of Denmark or Region Zealand and/or (ii) a scientist from the life science industry who fits your research interests and fulfil the programme requirements for Mentor Teams. We recommend that you have the Mentor Team preapproved in due time before application deadline 9 February 2027 by sending a request to BRIDGE: bridge@sund.ku.dk 	
• Alternatively, browse through the list of submitted project synopses (Open Mentor Teams) and find a Mentor Team that fits your research interests. Contact the suitable Mentor Team to explore the possibility of collaborating on a BRIDGE application. The list will be published on the BRIDGE website on 14 December 2026.   If you are an applicant without ties to the Faculty or hospitals in either of the two regions, please read more about our suggestions on how to proceed here.

  If you are in contact with a Mentor Team, we recommend that you:

   	
• Have the Mentor Team constellation preapproved in due time before the call closure by sending a request to BRIDGE: bridge@sund.ku.dk.   Read more about how to become a fellow.

   Application material

   	
• Part 1: Project description (must be co-designed by the applicant and Mentor Team) 	
• Part 2: Project abstract and CV (must be composed by the applicant independently) 	
• Part 3: Supplementary documents    Applications (Part 1, Part 2, and Part 3) must be submitted online through the link on the website no later than 9 February 2027, 23:59 CET. A cover letter is not needed, and there is no need for entering the application in NORMA. 

  Please find the requirements for the application and download the new and updated application templates.

  We reserve the right to disregard material received after the application deadline along with applications and application material that do not comply with the above-mentioned criteria. 

  Recruitment procedure  
 The received applications will be shortlisted and assessed according to the Ministry Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities 2012 and the University of Copenhagen’s guidelines 2013.  

  Upon the application deadline, the authorised recruitment manager will select applicants for assessment based on the advice of the Appointment Committee.

  All applicants will be notified on whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Assessment Committee will do a non-prioritised assessment based on the applicant’s academic qualifications and on the match between the fellow and the translational research project. All applicants will have the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant themselves (Part 2).

  Please find more information on the recruitment process for scientific personnel at the University of Copenhagen.

  Appointment interviews
 Following the completion of the assessments, a subset of candidates will be invited for a physical appointment interview with the Appointment Committee. The BRIDGE Programme will reimburse travel and accommodation expenses for invited applicants.

  The interviews are scheduled to take place 11-13 May 2027. Please note that Mentor Teams will need to be present online for a short introduction of the Mentor Team at this interview.

  Terms of employment
 The employment as Postdoc is fulltime (37 hours per week) and for two years. The start date is on 1 September 2027.

  Salary, pension, and terms of employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) and the Ministry of Finance. 

  The position is covered by the “Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at the Universities” of 2025.

  Financial composition of the fellowships
 The financing of running costs for the individual research projects will be covered by the hosting environments. Each fellow will in addition receive an annual sum of DKK 40,000 during their two-year employment to cover costs for PC, travel, language courses, conference and workshop participation and other relevant activities outside the programme.

  Successful fellowship recipients will be enrolled in the BRIDGE – Translational Excellence Programme and employed at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences at UCPH. Upon fulfilment of course participation and the individual research projects, fellows will be awarded a Certificate of Excellence.

Do you want to create something new? Do you want to fundamentally change how we organize teaching and learning at the SCIENCE departments? Do you want to be part of a unique opportunity in the largest university in Denmark? Then you might be our new SCIENCE Makerspace Operation Director.

  We invite applications for a 5-year position as Operation Director for the SCIENCE Makerspace at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. The Faculty of Science is committed to sustainably continuing the Makerspace activities at the end of the 5-year period, providing the possibility for extending the position long-term.

   

  About the SCIENCE Makerspace

  We are establishing a top-tier Makerspace at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen, spearheaded by the Department of Computer Science (DIKU), Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), and the Department of Science Education (IND). The SCIENCE Makerspace vision is built upon a foundation of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB) and aims to create an inclusive learning environment that bridges disciplines, supports different ways of learning, and attracts students with diverse backgrounds and interests. Everyone is welcome, and no prior knowledge of makerspaces, machines, or materials is required.

  The SCIENCE Makerspace will be established as a 600 sqm facility centrally located at Nørre Campus, with a budget of 42 million DKK over 5 years supported by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The Makerspace is expected to host 1-3 university courses per academic quarter, independent projects for BSc/MSc/PhD students, and be a venue for extracurricular workshops and 'blue sky' ideas from faculty and students. The Makerspace will also facilitate the integration between traditional and non-traditional forms of knowledge production within an Expert-in-residence program.

  The Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen is one of Scandinavia's largest science faculties, with over 4,000 staff, ~9,000 students, and an annual turnover exceeding DKK 3 billion, located in the heart of Copenhagen. SCIENCE hosts 12 departments spanning a breadth of disciplines from molecular biology and chemistry to mathematics, computer science, and geoscience, united by a commitment to curiosity-driven, high-impact research. 

   

  Description of the position

  We offer a unique opportunity for you to become the Operation Director of the ‘yet-to-be-build' 600 sqm SCIENCE Makerspace centrally placed at the Northen Campus in Copenhagen. The SCIENCE Makerspace vision is to design, build and run an inclusive and innovative learning space that bridges disciplines, allows for multi-modal learning activities, and attracts a diversified and balanced cohort of students from different educational programs (BSc, MSc, PhD) across the 12 Departments.

  The Operations Director will direct the SCIENCE Makerspace and be the manager for the Makerspace team. The Operation Director is responsible for ensuring that principles for DEIB are mainstreamed in all decisions in the Makerspace. 

  You will be part of the core decision-making on how to organize, establish, and run the ‘one-of-a-kind' Makerspace. You will collaborate with committed faculty from DIKU, NBI, and IND in the establishing phases, and with the Deanery for Education for long-term engagement across the departments in making the Makerspace vision a reality.

  You will be part of hiring the team who will run the makerspace together with you including Technical Lab Manager, Lab Technician, and a group of student mentors.

  This is a unique opportunity to be part of creating something new, in the largest university in Denmark, which fundamentally will change how we organize teaching and learning at the SCIENCE departments.

   

  You will need four core competences to succeed in the position:

   	
• You will need skills and expertise which allow you to strategize and develop ideas which will foster success for the SCIENCE Makerspace vision. This includes the work of identifying and understanding upcoming challenges for e.g. DEIB [DK3] (organizationally, socially, technically, and spatially) and finding solutions, while pro-actively execute required actions. Further, the Operation director must be able to function within an ‘entrepreneurial atmosphere’ where everything is not settled yet. 	
• You will need leadership and management competences which will allow you to lead a mixed Makerspace team of both highly skilled lab manager and lab technicians whose work requires levels of trust and autonomy, as well as student mentors who need clear instructions and guidance. 	
• You will need to navigate and understand the organizational and social structures of academia and university life, this includes considering the intrinsic motivation of researchers/teachers and PhD students, and how they might differ for MSc/BSc students. Such competence can arrive from your own experience during your education and does not require that you have worked in a university setting previously. 	
• You need interest in ‘making’ and Makerspaces. Furthermore, it is important that you consider consulting relevant experts about their views and perspectives, which will allow you to take qualitatively and well-founded decisions about our joint Makerspace.   You will not be a one-person army, instead you will have three main groups with different types of competences and experiences you can draw on in the position, including the Makerspace team, an experienced team of administrative management colleagues, and the Faculty of SCIENCE teaching committee.

  To read more about the vision, plans, and background for the SCIENCE Makerspace, please visit ucphmakerspace.dk

   

  Qualifications

  You are pro-active, find solutions where others see barriers, and are excited about being a core part of establishing, building, and running the brand-new SCIENCE Makerspace at University of Copenhagen, Denmark. 

  You have a relevant higher education or experience from similar positions. 

  You care for students and want to make it possible for all students at SCIENCE to experience learning activities where ‘making’ plays a role, e.g. as part of courses, project work, tech workshops, and extracurricular activities. 

  You are committed to the agenda of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB), know about Universal Design, and strongly believe that all activities and decisions in the pioneer SCIENCE Makerspace must take into account the multiple, intersecting dimensions of groups including, but not limited to genders, internationality, neurodiversity, socioeconomic backgrounds, and physical feasibility.

  Our ideal candidate can be described as:

   	
• Have management experience - potentially from a university or a politically governed organization. 	
• Demonstrates a high degree of trust under responsibility towards our employees, who are self-driven and accountable. As a manager, you help set the overall direction, contribute to daily well-being and cohesion, and support the development of individual employees and the team, while maintaining an overview of strategic initiatives in collaboration with your staff. 	
• Has an understanding of others’ work situations, you are able to develop strong collaborative relationships across employees with different educational and professional backgrounds. 	
• You have personal or professional making experience, pedagogical expertise and DEIB expertise 	
• You are structured, service-minded, approachable, and able to build commitment to strategic decisions. 	
• You thrive in a diverse environment with a wide variety of tasks. 	
• You have collaboration skills and the ability to build networks across professional groups, including across the organization 	
• You have strong communication skills in English (oral and written) and is ready to learn Danish.    

  Living in Copenhagen

  The university is situated in Copenhagen, which is consistently rated among the world's top 10 most livable cities. Located in Denmark, ranked in the top three happiest countries globally, Copenhagen boasts a vibrant culture, rich in music, theater, and community organizations. Life for families is made easier via a publicly supported daycare and healthcare system, dual-career opportunities, maternity/parental leave, and six weeks of annual vacation. International candidates may find information on living and working in Denmark. Useful information is also available at the university’s International Staff Mobility (ISM) office, which offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Terms of employment

  The Operation Director reports to the Head of Administration, Department of Computer Science, Camilla Lillholm. You will be employed as a senior consultant with managerial responsibility in accordance with the collective agreement for academics in the state sector. There is an opportunity to negotiate additional allowances based on qualifications.

  Note that Denmark protects the economic, social, and physical well-being of its workers, which includes robust health care, childcare, elder care, and other generous benefits. Thus, direct salary comparisons across nations are typically not meaningful.

   

  Further information

Are you ready to take the next step in your M&A career and work on some of the most exciting deals in the market? We are looking for a Senior Consultant to join our Transaction Strategy and Execution team in Copenhagen.

Shape your future with confidence.

Skills and attributes for success

You are analytically strong and comfortable working with complex data and problem-solving, using AI-enabled tools to enhance analysis and insight generation. You bring a structured and pragmatic approach, combined with strong business understanding and attention to detail.

You thrive in fast-paced environments and can manage ambiguity while maintaining focus on delivering high-quality outcomes. At the same time, you communicate clearly and confidently, translating complexity into actionable insights for both clients and colleagues.

You bring experience from client-facing or in-house roles across M&A execution (pre- and/or post-deal) and operational delivery, for example:

• Product and technology diligence

As a Senior Consultant, you will work across a range of M&A engagements spanning M&A strategy, operational diligence, as well as value creation and deal management. You are passionate about the operational aspects of M&A, thrive in fast-paced and ambiguous environments, and build trusted relationships with clients and colleagues.

• Managing and driving workstreams across pre- and post-deal engagements

What we look for

As our new colleague you bring 3-6 years of experience from strategy and M&A consulting or industry experience. You bring an inclusive approach, building strong relationships with both clients and colleagues and are a strong communicator who can translate complex ideas into clear and actionable insights. You take ownership of your work with a consistent focus on quality and impact.

• Work on complex, high-profile M&A and divestment engagements

• A purpose-led culture focused on creating long-term value for clients and society

EY | Building a better working world

EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

Full-Stack Software Engineer (Mid/Senior)

Location: Central Copenhagen; primarily in office

Language: English

Highlights:

• Full-Stack Python/TS engineer needed for a B2B SaaS startup in Copenhagen (with plenty of traction!)

• We have a lean, get-stuff-done team. No annoying extra management layers or unnecessary bureaucratic rituals. And we are "AI-forward" in our own development practices.

• You will own features end to end, from the data model through to the screen, on a platform that manufacturers rely on to keep production lines running.

• You will work in a small engineering team, directly with the person who decides what we build, and the problems you spend your time on are hard because the domain is hard, not because the organization is.

• We're building legitimately useful tools for the industries and companies that make the world go around.... manufacturers. Both AI-tools and just "plain-old-good-software" tools.

About Supplios

Manufacturers live or die by their supply base. Sourcing the wrong supplier, onboarding one slowly, failing to qualify one properly or losing track of a non-conformance can stop a production line and cost millions. Yet most manufacturers still run these relationships across email chains, spreadsheets and shared drives.

Supplios is a supplier collaboration platform for manufacturers in automotive and industrial sectors. We cover the full supplier relationship: sourcing, onboarding, qualification, day-to-day collaboration, compliance and supplier quality, all in a modern cloud based platform that is easy for manufacturers to implement and operate. It is built specifically for the way automotive and industrial manufacturers actually work.

We are headquartered in central Copenhagen and already serve customers globally in our vertical, including some of the most demanding names in automotive. We have grown to this point almost entirely on product strength, domain credibility and word of mouth.

The platform now covers more ground than the team that built it. We are hiring engineers to keep that pace sustainable, and to go deeper on the parts of the product our customers are pushing hardest.

The role

You will join a small engineering team and work across the whole stack: Python on the backend, TypeScript on the frontend and in the AI layers. There is no split between people who design and people who implement. You will take a problem from a customer conversation or a product decision through to something running in production for real manufacturers.

You will work directly with our co-founder and CEO, who is a hands-on product builder himself. That means short conversations instead of tickets thrown over a wall, and it means your questions about why something should work a certain way get answered by the person who decided it.

The domain is genuinely complicated, and that is the interesting part. Supplier relationships in automotive involve deep hierarchies, long-running approval processes, strict audit requirements and a lot of state that has to be exactly right. Modeling that well is most of the job.

Title and level flex with experience. We are open to strong mid-level engineers and to senior engineers who want more scope than their current company gives them.

We work together from our office in central Copenhagen. This is primarily an in-office role: at this stage, and on a codebase with this much implicit context, working through problems with the rest of the team in person is much faster than doing it in writing. Sensible flexibility when you need it is a given; full-time remote is not what we are offering.

Our current stack:

• Backend: Python / Django

• Frontend: Vue (but no specific Vue experience is needed)

• Infrastructure: AWS (mostly)

• Agents: Cloudflare (TypeScript) + Claude & OpenAI platform

What you will do

• Build features end to end, from data model and backend logic through to the TypeScript frontend our customers actually click on.

• Build end-to-end / front-to-back AI features (in-app AI assistants, background worker agents, email-routing agents, customer-configurable agent framework components)

• Design and evolve the relational data model that sits under supplier relationships, approvals and quality records.

• Take vaguely defined customer problems and turn them into something specific enough to build, then build it.

• Work on integrations between Supplios and customer systems (ERP and adjacent tooling), where failures have visible consequences for a production line.

• Improve the parts of the codebase that need it, rather than routing around them.

• Review other people's code and have yours reviewed; we keep the loop tight and unbureaucratic.

• Help keep the platform healthy in production across our regions: errors, performance and the boring things that keep customers trusting us.

• Take part in product decisions. Engineers here are expected to have opinions about what we build, not just how.

What we are looking for

Essential

• Professional experience with Python. This is not negotiable; the backend is Python and you need to be effective in it.

• Solid TypeScript experience and genuine comfort working on the frontend.

• Experience building and running SaaS products, including the part after launch where real users depend on them.

• AI-forward development techniques. (This does not mean you no longer write code.)

• A track record of owning work end to end without waiting to be told what to do next.

• The temperament for a small, senior company: high ownership, low ceremony.

• You want to work primarily from an office in central Copenhagen, with a small team.

Nice to have

Genuinely a plus, not a requirement. Nobody has all of these.

• Experience with B2B enterprise SaaS, especially where customers are large and demanding and implementations are not self-serve. This is a significant plus.

• Experience with complex relational data modeling, and with large, long-lived codebases that you did not write yourself. A big plus.

• Experience building AI-based products, using the latest frameworks/harnesses and infrastructure components (including RAG) is a significant plus.

• Familiarity with any of: domain-driven design, the actor model, finite state machines, CQRS, event-driven architecture. We use these ideas where they earn their place, and it helps if the vocabulary is already yours.

• Startup experience, particularly early stage. A significant plus.

• Knowledge of manufacturing, automotive or supply chain. Useful, but we can teach you the domain; we cannot teach you the craft, so do not rule yourself out on this.

Language

English is the only important language for this position; we work in English, and so do our customers. Danish language skills are not required.

Why this role is worth your time

• The scope is unusually large for the stage. You are one of a small number of engineers on a platform that serves demanding customers globally. What you build ships, and it ships soon.

• No layers between you and the decisions. You work directly with the co-founder and CEO, who runs product. There is no committee to navigate and nobody to translate your work for you.

• Hard problems that are not artificially hard. The complexity comes from the domain (hierarchies, state, audit trails, integrations that must not fail), not from organisational overhead.

• Real customers already, and real gaps. The product has paying customers in automotive and clear places where it needs to get better. Both halves of that are true, and both are why this is a good job.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note on why this role interests you to team@supplios.com. Work examples will help.

Apply by email

Send an email to team@supplios.com

Please include your CV / resume, and a brief note about why you're interested in the position.

Thanks!
